items.summary: S186-S188 added 13 funnel beacons to the Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS allowlist (studio-dispatch:subscribe, proof-line:{shown,click}, play-next:{shown,click}, oracle-chip:{shown,click}, ignis-hint:{shown,dismissed,click}). They fire from real pages to /v/rum and are allowlist-verified by the S188 gate. But rollup-rum.mjs aggregates ONLY web-vitals (lcpP75/fcpP75/... per route) and discards every ux event name. The funnel is instrumented at the edge and blind at the analysis layer — the studio measures uptime, LCP, and AI-spine health as /status/ tiles, but cannot see its own conversion funnel.
items.why: This is the same silent-drop class as the S186 RUM bug, one layer deeper: the names are allowlisted and emitted, but nothing aggregates them, so the data dies in the rollup. Closing it answers the only question that decides whether S186-S188 paid off: which funnel step leaks. Build it honest-dark (matches the S178 field-win pattern) so it lands now and lights up as CI accrues samples, and prove the aggregation logic this session with a synthetic-fixture self-test even if live counts are sparse.
items.recipe: Add scripts/rollup-rum-ux.mjs (self-test on synthetic samples) that reads the SAME raw pulled sample dir as rollup-rum.mjs, aggregates ux event counts by name per day, writes data/rum-ux-history.ndjson + public-safe api/funnel-summary.json (anonymous aggregate COUNTS only — no email/PII, cost-neutral per CANON-029, honest-dark when total<N). Chain it into the npm run rum:pull sequence after rollup-rum. Add a /status/ 'Conversion funnel' tile rendering visit -> dispatch-shown -> dispatch-subscribe -> proof-line-click -> membership-intent as a step-leak bar. Add scripts/check-funnel-contract.mjs (shape + drift gate) to build + build:check. Outcome: the founder finally sees the funnel's leak points.
items.outcome: conversion-measurement: surfaces which funnel step (capture -> subscribe -> intent) leaks, turning the 3-session funnel build from unproven to tunable.

items.summary: Ask IGNIS / the Oracle answer engine delivers answers blind — there is no signal on whether an answer actually helped. S186 seeded one-tap question chips (killing the cold-start) and instrumented hint shown/click, but the ANSWER itself has no helpful/unhelpful capture, so the studio can't tell a great retrieval answer from a useless one, and the oracle-insights clustering has no quality gradient to learn from.
items.why: A retrieval answer with no feedback affordance is a dead-end for both the visitor (no way to say 'that missed') and the studio (no way to improve ranking). A single 1-tap helpful/unhelpful control closes the AI feedback loop, feeds the new funnel-summary as an 'answer helpfulness' info-finding metric, and respects the established pattern: allowlist the beacon, let the S188 check-rum-allowlist gate verify both ends stay in sync.
items.recipe: In assets/ignis-answer-engine.js, render a compact 'Helpful? thumbs up / thumbs down' control under each delivered answer (CSS classes, no inline styles per the strict style gate). On tap, emit allowlisted oracle-answer:{helpful,unhelpful} via the existing emitUx/beacon path and hide the control. Add oracle-answer:helpful + oracle-answer:unhelpful to Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS, then run node scripts/check-rum-allowlist.mjs so emit<->allowlist stays in sync. Surface the helpful-rate in funnel-summary (item #1) so answer quality is measured, not guessed.
items.outcome: info-finding quality: makes Oracle answer helpfulness a measured signal and gives visitors a way to flag a miss, feeding future cluster ranking.
